title: Mandukya Upanishad (12 verses, one week): the four states; om, letter by letter (7 of 7)
hook: the fourth has no letter: the silence after om, and four weeks of Upanishads
tomorrow: Karma yoga deep-dive: action as offering; Karma Yoga as taught by Vivekananda; work as worship (1 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Mandukya Upanishad: om, letter by letter. A is waking, u is dream, m is deep sleep. And the fourth has no letter. Today, why. Day two hundred fifty-nine.

Musicians say the rests matter as much as the notes. A song with no silence in it is just noise. The pause before the last chorus, the beat of quiet after the final chord, that's where the music lands. The Mandukya has given three of its quarters a sound: a, u, m. The last verse is about the one that doesn't get one. And it closes this whole four-week stretch of the Upanishads with a rest.
screen: `THE RESTS MATTER.` → `THREE QUARTERS HAVE A SOUND.` → `THE LAST ONE DOESN'T.`

segments.voice: Verse twelve: the fourth is without a letter, amatra. Beyond all dealings. The world comes to rest in it. Auspicious. Not two. So om is the self. The one who knows this enters the self by the self. That's the end of the Upanishad. The fourth isn't a fourth sound after m. It's the silence the whole syllable rises out of and falls back into. That's why teachers ask you to rest after chanting om: the silence isn't the end of the practice; it's the point. And the last line is lovely: you enter the self by the self. Not by going somewhere else. By being what you already are. Now look back at the week. Om is all this, past, present, future, and beyond. The self is Brahman, with four quarters. Waking, knowing outward. Dream, the shining one, lit from within. Deep sleep, a mass of knowing, made of bliss. The fourth: peaceful, auspicious, not two. The letters a, u, m. And the silence with no letter at all. And look back at the four weeks. The Isha: all this is pervaded by the Lord; renounce and enjoy. The Kena: by whom does the mind move? The one behind the ear, and the gods who learned their victory wasn't theirs. The Katha: a boy at Death's door choosing the good over the pleasant. The Mandukya: the fourth. Four short texts, and every one points to the same place, behind the eye, underneath the three states, closer than breath. Next, three weeks on the three paths the Gita laid out: action, devotion and knowledge.
screen: `THE FOURTH HAS NO LETTER.` · `THE WORLD COMES TO REST.` · `ENTER THE SELF BY THE SELF.` · `ISHA, KENA, KATHA, MANDUKYA.` · then, large: `THE FOURTH.`

segments.voice: Two minutes. Yesterday you chanted the letters; today, start where they end. Breathe out slowly, all the way. At the bottom of the out-breath, before the next breath begins, there's a small pause that nobody made. Rest there. Let the in-breath come by itself. Each time the breath empties, meet the pause again. Don't stretch it; just notice it. If a thought arrives, let it fade the way a sound does. If you'd like, chant om once at the start and let it fall into that same pause. The bell holds the time.
The Mandukya Upanishad. Twelve verses: om is all this; the self has four quarters; a, u, m for three of them, and silence for the fourth.

Your line: the fourth. That's the week, and the Upanishads. Tomorrow, the first of the three paths: work. Today, once, when a conversation goes quiet, let the pause stay a pause. Day two hundred fifty-nine.

screen: `DAY 259 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: KARMA YOGA, ACTION AS OFFERING.`

howItsDone: Hindu practitioners who chant om are often taught to rest in the silence after the syllable, which the Mandukya's twelfth verse identifies with the fourth, the self beyond waking, dream and deep sleep.

match.prompt: four weeks, four Upanishads — tap the pairs.
pairs: choose the good over the pleasant

myth: the fourth is a fourth sound after a, u and m
it's amatra, without a letter: the silence om rises from and returns to.
the Mandukya ends: the one who knows this enters the self by the self
not by going elsewhere; by being what you already are.

fork.setup: you've chanted a, u, m. what does the Mandukya say about the fourth?
options: it has no letter; it's the silence.
fork.reveal: the fourth is without a letter: beyond dealings, the world at rest, auspicious, not two.

original.note: Sanskrit: amatra, without measure, without a letter; Mandukya 12's word for the fourth.

trapdoor: what you thought: the chant ends when the sound stops.
what it means: in the Mandukya, the silence after om is the fourth, the point of the whole syllable.
what a scholar hears: Mandukya 12 (amatrash caturtho 'vyavaharyah prapancopashamah shivo 'dvaita) repeats verse 7's terms, closing the text in a ring.

sources.ref: Mandukya Upanishad 12 (the fourth is without a letter; enter the self by the self)
